quests.question:
The two suppliers both sent samples, and they were delivered on the same day.
What is 'they' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: The two suppliers both sent samples, and they were delivered on the same day.
quests.hint: The passive verb 'were delivered' points to what travels.
quests.explanation: The pronoun 'they' is plural, but the suppliers are people who sent things. What was delivered on the same day is the samples.

quests.question:
Kabir and Anya both applied, but only he was invited to interview.
Who is 'he' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Kabir and Anya both applied, but only he was invited to interview.
quests.explanation: 'Both' covers Kabir and Anya, but 'he' picks out one. It is Kabir, the male applicant.

quests.question:
Both of the printers ran out of toner, so neither of them worked until the caretaker replaced it.
What is meant by 'them'?
quests.sentence: Both of the printers ran out of toner, so neither of them worked until the caretaker replaced it.
quests.explanation: 'Both of the printers' establishes the pair. 'Neither of them' picks up the same pair.

quests.question:
The guard told us that all the passengers had to have their seat belts checked before take-off.
Whose seat belts does 'their' refer to?
quests.sentence: The guard told us that all the passengers had to have their seat belts checked before take-off.
quests.explanation: 'Their' is plural and belongs to those being checked. The passengers own the belts; the guard is not one.

quests.question:
Some of the tickets were sold online, and they cost less than those bought at the door.
Which tickets does 'they' refer to?
quests.sentence: Some of the tickets were sold online, and they cost less than those bought at the door.
options: the tickets bought at the door
quests.hint: 'Those bought at the door' is the comparison. What is cheaper?
quests.explanation: Look closely: 'they' is the subject compared with 'those bought at the door'. The comparison implies the online tickets.

quests.question:
Some of the milk had spilled, but it hadn't reached the floor.
What is meant by 'it'?
quests.sentence: Some of the milk had spilled, but it hadn't reached the floor.
quests.explanation: 'It' is singular and refers to the substance that spilled. The floor is where it might have gone, not what did the spilling.

quests.question:
The guard reminded us that every employee must show their card at the gate.
Who is meant by 'their'?
quests.sentence: The guard reminded us that every employee must show their card at the gate.
quests.explanation: 'Their' is the singular 'they', matching 'every employee'. The guard is giving the reminder.

quests.question:
Every dish on the menu comes with a side, and you can swap it for salad.
What does 'it' refer to?
quests.sentence: Every dish on the menu comes with a side, and you can swap it for salad.
quests.hint: What can be swapped for salad?
quests.explanation: Consider the form of 'it': it is singular and refers to the item that can be swapped. That is the side, not the whole dish or menu.

quests.question:
Every student got a certificate, and each one was signed by the principal herself.
Who is 'herself' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Every student got a certificate, and each one was signed by the principal herself.
quests.explanation: 'Herself' emphasises the person who signed. The principal is the singular, feminine noun who did it.

quests.question:
Many of the residents signed the petition, and several have since asked the organisers to remove their names.
In this text, who does 'their' stand for?
quests.sentence: Many of the residents signed the petition, and several have since asked the organisers to remove their names.
quests.hint: Whose names appear on the petition and are now being withdrawn?
quests.explanation: 'Their names' are the names of the people who signed. Several of the residents are the ones asking for removal, whereas the organisers only receive the request.

quests.question:
Many tourists visit the temple, but few of them stay long enough to see the gardens behind it.
What is being referred to by 'it'?
quests.sentence: Many tourists visit the temple, but few of them stay long enough to see the gardens behind it.
quests.hint: 'It' is singular. What are the gardens behind?
quests.explanation: In this sentence, 'it' is singular and non-human, so it is not 'many tourists'. The gardens are behind the temple.

quests.question:
The nurse checked on the patients, and a few of them needed extra blankets.
Who is being referred to by 'them'?
quests.sentence: The nurse checked on the patients, and a few of them needed extra blankets.
quests.explanation: 'A few of them' picks a subset from a group. The group is the patients; the nurse is one person and blankets are needed by people.

quests.question:
We compared two offers. Either would work, but neither of them includes travel.
What is meant by 'them'?
quests.sentence: We compared two offers. Either would work, but neither of them includes travel.
quests.hint: 'Neither of them' picks from a pair.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of them' refers back to the pair. The two offers are the things being compared.

quests.question:
Neither Ivan nor Paula answered, but the message I left for them was clear.
Who is meant by 'them'?
quests.sentence: Neither Ivan nor Paula answered, but the message I left for them was clear.
quests.explanation: With 'neither... nor', the plural pronoun 'them' still refers to both people. The message was left for both.

quests.question:
There are two candidates, and either could win if their supporters turn out.
Who is being referred to by 'their'?
quests.sentence: There are two candidates, and either could win if their supporters turn out.
quests.hint: 'Either' can point to each candidate. Whose supporters?
quests.explanation: In this sentence, 'their' refers to the candidates, since it is they who have supporters. The supporters are the ones who turn out.

quests.question:
The workshop had thirty participants, some of whom had travelled overnight.
What does 'whom' point back to?
quests.sentence: The workshop had thirty participants, some of whom had travelled overnight.
quests.explanation: 'Some of whom' takes a subset from a group of people. The group is the participants.

quests.question:
The library received two hundred donations, most of which were textbooks.
What does 'which' point back to?
quests.sentence: The library received two hundred donations, most of which were textbooks.
quests.hint: 'Most of which' picks a majority. Of what?
quests.explanation: 'Most of which' refers to the group just mentioned, the donations. Textbooks are what most of them were.

quests.question:
The union represents drivers, all of whom must renew their licences every five years.
What is being referred to by 'whom'?
quests.sentence: The union represents drivers, all of whom must renew their licences every five years.
quests.hint: Which noun is a group of people?
quests.explanation: 'All of whom' points to the group of people mentioned before. The union is an organisation, so it would need 'which'.

quests.question:
The board is divided, but it has agreed to publish its report.
What does 'it' refer to?
quests.sentence: The board is divided, but it has agreed to publish its report.
quests.hint: A collective noun that takes a singular verb goes with a singular pronoun.
quests.explanation: A collective noun that takes 'is' is matched with singular 'it'. The board acts as one body here.

quests.question:
The team have all been given new laptops, and they are delighted.
Who is 'they' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: The team have all been given new laptops, and they are delighted.
quests.explanation: 'They' is plural and refers to the members of the team, who are the ones to be delighted.

quests.question:
The jury has reached its verdict, but the judge asked it to reconsider.
What does 'it' refer to?
quests.sentence: The jury has reached its verdict, but the judge asked it to reconsider.
quests.hint: Who reached the decision, and who was asked to reconsider?
quests.explanation: 'It' is singular, and the jury is treated as one unit here. The judge is the one asking.

quests.question:
Every participant received a name tag and was asked to wear it all day.
In this text, what does 'it' stand for?
quests.sentence: Every participant received a name tag and was asked to wear it all day.
quests.explanation: Remember that 'it' is singular and non-human, so it is not the participant. A name tag is the thing you wear.

quests.question:
Most of the staff are in on Fridays, but some work from home when they have deadlines.
Who is meant by 'they'?
quests.sentence: Most of the staff are in on Fridays, but some work from home when they have deadlines.
quests.explanation: 'But' contrasts the majority with the minority. 'They' refers to the subject of that clause, some.

quests.question:
None of the trainees passed the test, but the examiner said all of them could retake it next month.
What is meant by 'it'?
quests.sentence: None of the trainees passed the test, but the examiner said all of them could retake it next month.
quests.explanation: Here, 'it' is singular and non-human. What is retaken is the test, not the people or the examiner.

quests.question:
All of the guests had arrived except the Hendersons, who had sent word that they would be late.
Who is being referred to by 'they'?
quests.sentence: All of the guests had arrived except the Hendersons, who had sent word that they would be late.
quests.explanation: Notice that 'who' points to the Hendersons, and 'they' is the subject of the message. The other guests had already arrived.

quests.question:
Several of the interns asked their mentors for feedback, and most of them received it within days.
In this text, who does 'them' stand for?
quests.sentence: Several of the interns asked their mentors for feedback, and most of them received it within days.
quests.explanation: 'Most of them' takes a subset of a group. The recipients of feedback are the interns.

quests.question:
Several bidders submitted offers, and the seller accepted the highest, which was well above the estimate.
What is meant by 'which'?
quests.sentence: Several bidders submitted offers, and the seller accepted the highest, which was well above the estimate.
quests.explanation: 'Which' comments on the phrase just before it, the highest offer. The seller did the accepting.

quests.question:
Neither of the two banks would lend us money unless we could offer collateral, which we did not have.
What is 'which' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Neither of the two banks would lend us money unless we could offer collateral, which we did not have.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to the thing just before it, collateral. The banks and the money are not what was missing.

quests.question:
Many of the visitors asked the guide questions, and she answered all of them patiently.
What is 'them' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Many of the visitors asked the guide questions, and she answered all of them patiently.
quests.explanation: 'All of them' takes a whole set. She answers questions, not people, so 'them' is the questions.

quests.question:
Each of the co-authors read the draft, and every one of them suggested changes that the editor merged herself.
Who does 'herself' refer to?
quests.sentence: Each of the co-authors read the draft, and every one of them suggested changes that the editor merged herself.
quests.explanation: 'Herself' emphasises the person who did the merging. The editor is the singular, female subject.
